evidence: The dark upper number is 53: the second digit turns back at its right-hand join rather than having a continuous descending diagonal of 2. Its form is compatible with the authorial sequence 51, 52, 53, 54 on these leaves. Retain 53 as authorial numbering, not a marginal annotation.

Each superscript has the same crossed X or forked Y construction as the corresponding lower capital, reduced only by its superscript position. Both free waves and the single right-pointing arrow are visible; retain tilde X and tilde Y.
After the looped d, the final letter has an open u trough and upward join, not an enclosed e loop. Retain du.

The first group is the low o-n of on. The following continuous word has a looped d, low e-v-r-a, dotted i and final t. The overlapping short strokes are internal retracing, without a separate cancellation across fait or soit. Retain live devrait.

The initial letter of the abbreviation has a long returning g descender, not the straight q descender of que. The compact following run supports gén and ends at a detached point. The first abbreviation remains.
The Pi expression starts appreciably below the top of the large B and is attached as its subscript. It has a flat cap, two straight posts and the parenthesized capital X. No extra index 1 is written.

The whole word and group expression are cancelled. A q-like initial loop survives; the following strokes are too obscured to choose e rather than i at the end. Add qui to the existing doubtful que. The superscript remains tilde X/tilde alpha because its loop overlaps the cancellation; the smaller shape is not independently a lowercase x.

In (7), the two X shapes in the ordered pair share the same crossing and capital scale; the raised terminal X repeats that form under its wave. The arrow has a barred tail and right head. Retain the capitals and mapsto.

The point sign remains the same reduced zeta/xi form, with reversed preference alone in the second reading. The t of the short pt form is raised relative to the p body, supporting the retained superscript convention. The final horizontal stroke is the written dash.
The thin lower foliation clearly reads 106, including the closed lower loop of 6. It is distinct from the dark authorial page 53 and remains a margin entry.
